headline: Soybean and Wheat Funds Fall as Dollar Jumps Against Brazilian Real
summary: The soybean fund SOYB fell 1.23% and the wheat fund WEAT dropped 1.27% on Monday as the dollar surged 8.79% against Brazil's real, making local crops cheaper abroad.
why: Commodity funds provide investors with exposure to agricultural futures without directly trading physical grain. Currency fluctuations between the US dollar and emerging market currencies heavily impact global export competitiveness.

impacts.name: Teucrium Soybean Fund
impacts.why: Declined by 1.23% as a stronger US dollar against the Brazilian real made crops cheaper abroad.

impacts.name: Teucrium Wheat Fund
impacts.why: Fell 1.27% amid currency shifts impacting export pricing dynamics.

why_moved: The appreciation of the US dollar against the Brazilian real reduced the cost of Brazilian crops on international markets, putting downward pressure on US agricultural commodity funds.
